t: Beijing began as the walled city of Ji, a frontier seat on the northern edge of China proper, and was a provincial town for about a thousand years.
It became a capital under the Jin in 1153, the Mongol Yuan from 1271 and the Ming from 1421, which gave it the plan and monuments it still has.
It was named Ji, Youzhou, Nanjing, Zhongdu, Dadu, Beiping and Beijing, and its name and standing changed again in 1928, 1937 and 1949.
dyk: Beijing, the Northern Capital, took its name in 1403 to distinguish it from Nanjing, the Southern Capital. It lost the name in 1928, regained it under Japanese occupation in 1937, lost it again in 1945 and recovered it in 1949.
ev: The Zhou confer the city states of Ji and Yan, the date being the Beijing Government's official estimate
The Liao rename Youzhou Nanjing and make it a secondary capital
The Jin move their capital to Yanjing and name it Zhongdu
Kublai Khan founds the Yuan dynasty and names his capital Dadu
The Yongle Emperor renames Beiping as Beijing
The Manchus take the city and make it the seat of the Qing dynasty
The Eight-Nation Alliance lifts the siege of the Legation Quarter and occupies the city
Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen

f.founded: The city states of Ji and Yan were given to their rulers by King Wu of Zhou in the 11th century BCE according to Sima Qian; the Beijing Government uses 1045 BCE as the official estimate of the date
f.where: On the northern edge of the North China Plain, with mountains on three sides, near the Yongding River, in northern China
f.known: The Forbidden City; capital under the Jin, Yuan, Ming and Qing; Dadu of Kublai Khan; the Temple of Heaven; the Legation Quarter; the May Fourth Movement; Tiananmen Square; the Beijing dialect
f.today: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China and a provincial-level municipality with 16 districts.
